svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.13.13 Fire Dampers
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Fire Dampers

g.text: Duct through a rated fire separation: a fire
Branch duct under 130 cm² (20.2 in²), melting
air-conditioning units discharging at 1.2 m or less
Branch duct into an upward exhaust riser:
carried up inside at least 500 mm (19 11/16″),
Ducts into a vertical service space, melting
straight outside at the top: no damper

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
A duct that penetrates an assembly required to be a fire
separation with a fire-resistance rating is equipped with a
fire damper in conformance with Articles 3.1.8.4. and
Except as permitted by Sentences (2) to (5), 9.10.5.1.(3) and
A fire damper is not required where a noncombustible branch
duct pierces a required fire separation, provided the duct
(a) has a melting point not below 760°C (1400°F), (b) has a
cross-sectional area less than 130 cm² (20.2 in²), and (c) supplies
only air-conditioning units or combined air-conditioning and
heating units discharging air at not more than 1.2 m (3′-11¼″)
above the floor.
A fire damper is not required where a noncombustible branch
duct pierces a required fire separation around an exhaust duct
riser in which the airflow is upward, provided
(a) the branch duct melting point is not below 760°C (1400°F), (b)
the branch duct is carried up inside the riser not less than 500 mm
(19 11/16″), and (c) the exhaust duct is under negative pressure as
in Article 9.10.9.20.
Noncombustible ducts penetrating a fire separation around a
vertical service space need no fire damper at that fire
separation, provided
(a) their melting point is above 760°C (1400°F), and (b) each
individual duct exhausts directly to the outside at the top of the
vertical service space.
A duct serving commercial cooking equipment and piercing a
required fire separation need not have a fire damper at the
fire separation
See also Article 6.3.1.6.
Drawn: close-ups and slices, some walls see-through. Red: fire separations. Sentence (5) is in the panel.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.13.13. (page 9-79)
